answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the cedar identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator pays for 250 runs and collects one. Because the plume index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the nadir audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 250 answers need 250 separate inference runs with separate seeds. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
